asDecan.p: Each sign is cut into three slices of ten degrees, the decans, and each slice has a planet of its own and a small card to go with it. Your Sun sits in the first ten degrees of Leo. In the Golden Dawn order that slice goes to Saturn, which is an odd planet to find there. Leo is ruled by the Sun and it's fixed fire, warm and proud and made to be looked at. Saturn's home is Aquarius, the sign directly opposite, so in Leo it's in detriment, which just means it's working against the grain of the place and you can see the effort. The next slice along is Jupiter's, the Six of Wands, with the laurel wreath and the parade. After that comes Mars and the Seven, a man on a ridge fending everyone off. Yours comes before the parade. Strength is your Sun card, the broad picture of Leo, and the Five of Wands is the finer grain inside it.

You rarely get to coast on charm, and you stopped expecting to a long time ago. Before a job interview you've over-prepared, with notes on the company's last three annual reports, because some part of you assumes you'll have to win the room before it warms to you. At a family dinner, when your brother tells the story of the holiday and gets the laugh, you're the one quietly correcting the dates. You notice who got thanked in the all-staff email, and if it wasn't you, that sits with you for the rest of the afternoon. At a friend's wedding you're half listening to the speech and half rewriting your own. There's plenty of Leo pride in all this, but Saturn makes it do its homework first. You want to be seen, and you'd honestly prefer to be seen for something you sweated over.

What people tend to miss is that you're a very good sparring partner. Put you in a room of strong opinions, a writers' room, a school committee, a netball team with three people who all want to be captain, and you'll argue hard and then shake hands at the end without carrying a grudge home. Look at the picture on your card. Five lads swinging long sticks at each other and nobody's bleeding. You seem to understand that kind of fight in your bones. You also make the people around you better. A colleague who sits next to you for a year usually leaves sharper, partly because you pushed back on their draft and partly because they saw how much went into yours. And you can take a hard note. If an editor tells you the second half doesn't work, you'll sulk for an evening and have it rewritten by Wednesday.

The less obvious trouble is what happens once the recognition actually turns up. You've spent so long expecting to fight for it that when it's simply handed over, a promotion, a round of applause, a friend saying your lasagne is the best they've had, you don't quite trust it. You find the flaw, or decide they're only being kind, and the goalposts move again. The other thing is that you can make a contest out of moments that don't have one. Your partner mentions a good week at work and you find yourself listing yours. A friend gets engaged and some small, ungenerous part of you checks where you are against them. You're not proud of that and you'd never say it out loud, but it's there, and the people closest to you can sometimes feel it in the room.

When things go wrong you dig in and work harder. You get passed over, or a relationship ends, or a project you'd put a year into gets shelved, and your first move is to prove somebody made a mistake. Longer hours, a new course, a gym membership, a very well-formatted spreadsheet. A week on, the heat has usually gone out of it and you're tired and flat, and you've stopped mentioning it to anyone, because Leo hates being seen to struggle and Saturn tells you it's your own job to fix. So the people around you get a version of you that's polite and shut, which can be harder on them than a row would be. What helps is letting one person see the wobble before you've sorted it. After that, something with nothing to win in it, a swim, cooking for friends, a film you've seen ten times.

You don't fall in love lightly, and you don't much like being picked by accident. Early on you can come across as warm but careful, checking whether the other person is serious before you let the big Leo generosity out. Once it's out it's a lot. The planned birthdays, the loyalty, the way you'll back them up at a party whether they were right or not. What partners find harder is the scorekeeping you don't know you're doing. Who apologised last, who made more effort at Christmas, who texted first after the argument. You also need to be told you're appreciated far more often than you'll ever ask, and a partner who assumes you just know can leave you quietly going without for months. If you want to hear it, say so. Something like "I'd like to hear you're proud of me" is a perfectly reasonable thing to ask for.

You're built for work where there's a standard to meet and someone to measure yourself against. Competitive fields suit a lot of people with this decan, law, sales, sport, the performing arts, anywhere with an audition or a pitch or a table of results at the end of the quarter. You do your best stuff when a rival is doing good stuff at the next desk, and a quiet office with nobody to compare against can leave you oddly flat. Bosses usually notice you're thorough before they notice you're talented, which annoys you. You're also often the one who stays back to fix the slides the night before the big presentation, and then minds a great deal when someone else gets up and gives it. Raise that before the meeting. Say plainly that you want your name on the work, because Saturn in Leo will otherwise wait years to be noticed.

At twenty this decan is often all effort and very little ease. You're auditioning for everything, a bit prickly about rejection, and inclined to think anyone who got there faster must have had help. It's a hard age for Saturn in Leo because the recognition hasn't had time to arrive yet. By the mid-thirties the picture usually shifts. The years of work start to show, as a reputation or a skill people pay for, and most people with this slice of Leo begin competing with their own last effort and stop watching the person at the next desk so closely. The fifties are often kind here, since Saturn tends to do its best work late. A lot of early Leos I've seen end up as the coach or mentor in their field, the one who tells a young talent their draft isn't ready and then stays late helping them fix it.

Once a week, on the same evening, write down one thing you did well that nobody saw or thanked you for. The report you checked twice, the call you made to your aunt, the argument you decided not to start. Just a line, in the same notebook every time. On the first of each month, read one entry out loud to someone you trust and let them say something nice about it. Don't correct them or play it down. Say thanks and change the subject.
